orchestrate.description: Heavy multi-agent feature build: scout -> plan -> implement -> adversarial review -> verify -> iterate. For multi-file features; for single-file work stay in build and use @oracle + /checks. Takes over the current session — run it from a fresh one. Usage: /orchestrate <feature description>
orchestrate.template:
You are the orchestrator. Load and follow the 'orchestration-loop' skill precisely. The feature request to implement is:

$ARGUMENTS

Begin immediately with Phase 1 (scouting). Only ask for clarification if the goal is genuinely ambiguous — one focused question, then proceed regardless.

checks.description: Run every check in .agents/checks/ against the diff, one subagent each, in parallel. Codified conventions — complements the built-in /review, which covers general correctness. Usage: /checks [scope]
checks.template:
Run the project's review checks in parallel. You are the aggregator only — you do NOT review any code yourself.

1. DETERMINE SCOPE. If the following is non-empty, use it as the scope (a git ref range, `--staged`, a commit hash, or a path): $ARGUMENTS
   Otherwise use `git diff`. If that is empty use `git diff --staged`. If that is also empty use `git show HEAD`. Also run `git status --short` to catch untracked files — they are part of the change and no diff will show them. State the resolved scope in one line.

2. COLLECT CHECKS. Glob `.agents/checks/*.md` under the project root and `~/.agents/checks/*.md`. Read each one. A project check overrides a global check with the same `name` in its frontmatter.

3. DISPATCH. Issue ONE `task` call per check, and issue them ALL IN THE SAME RESPONSE so they run in parallel. Use `subagent_type: "reviewer"`. Each brief must contain: the check's `name`, its `severity-default`, the check body VERBATIM (do not summarize it), and the exact scope commands to run. If no check files exist anywhere, say so and stop — do not invent a review, the built-in /review already covers general correctness.

4. AGGREGATE. Group findings by severity: critical, high, medium, low. Drop exact duplicates at the same file:line. Name any check that returned `clean`. Do not add findings of your own, do not soften or reword a finding, and do not fix anything — this is a report.

5. End with a one-line verdict: total findings by severity, and whether anything blocks a commit (critical or high does; medium and low do not).
